--- explanation ---
# 2026 Spanish Grand Prix (MADRING) pre-race forecast

**Forecast cut-off:** 13 September 2026, approximately 07:30 UTC (race start 13:00 UTC).

## Evidence used

- The FIA provisional grid puts Norris, Antonelli, Verstappen, Hamilton, Leclerc, Russell, Piastri and Lawson in the first eight places. Sainz drops to P20 for impeding Bottas; Bearman and Stroll are permitted to start P21/P22; Stroll has a 40-place power-unit penalty. [FIA Document 57](https://www.fia.com/system/files/decision-document/2026_spanish_grand_prix_-_provisional_starting_grid.pdf) and [permission-to-start decision](https://www.fia.com/system/files/decision-document/2026_spanish_grand_prix_-_decision_-_permission_to_start.pdf).
- Norris beat Antonelli by only 0.011 seconds in Q3, with Verstappen 0.140s from pole and the first seven covered by 0.470s. Earlier phases and all three practices pointed more strongly toward Mercedes than Norris's exceptional final lap alone. [Official qualifying report](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/norris-denies-antonelli-pole-position-for-spanish-gp-in-closely-fought-qualifying-in-madrid.5AqJXaE8s1sLfv8dJVLqty).
- Friday's short, traffic-affected long runs made Russell the benchmark. Motorsport's compound/stint-adjusted analysis had Verstappen about 0.13s per lap behind, Antonelli 0.55s behind, the Ferraris around 0.9s behind and Piastri 1.51s behind. Norris had no representative high-fuel run after a gearbox problem. [Motorsport.com long-run analysis](https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/mercedes-clearly-ahead-how-long-run-pace-compared-in-f1-spanish-gp-practice-/10854723/).
- The strategic evidence is unusually uncertain. Pirelli measured roughly 0.2–0.3s/lap degradation and front-left graining, but the green-flag pit loss is about 24 seconds and overtaking was extremely difficult in the support races. Medium-Hard is the natural one-stop; Medium-Hard-Hard remains competitive if Friday's degradation persists. [F1 team/Pirelli Saturday comments](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/what-the-teams-said-qualifying-in-spain-2026.014qyfNipmqu7dP0ZuCvfc) and [strategy analysis](https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/f1-teams-face-big-madring-strategy-dilemma/).
- The race is forecast to be hot, clear and dry, around 32°C ambient with a possible 53°C track temperature. [Motorsport.com weather preview](https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/f1-spanish-gp-at-madring-sunday-schedule-weather-forecast-and-how-to-watch/10855127/).
- Post-qualifying market prices were used as an external calibration rather than as the model itself. At the cut-off, the liquid Polymarket mid-prices were approximately Antonelli 40%, Norris 35%, Verstappen 12%, Hamilton 6.5%, Russell 4.45%, Leclerc 2.9% and Piastri 1.7% before normalization; sportsbook prices showed a similar front-row concentration. [Polymarket event](https://polymarket.com/event/f1-spanish-grand-prix-winner-2026-09-13) and [post-qualifying odds snapshot](https://www.thespread.com/auto-racing/2026-f1-spanish-grand-prix-predictions-and-picks-our-best-bets-for-madring/).

## Method and interpretation

I combined the 13 completed 2026 Grands Prix, recent form, grid position, weekend pace and driver/team reliability in a Monte Carlo rank model. Because this is MADRING's first Grand Prix, outcomes were mixed across three latent race shapes: a track-position-led one-stop race, a high-degradation strategic race, and a Safety Car/red-flag-heavy race. Team-level pace uncertainty, starts, strategy errors, non-terminal incidents and correlated race conditions broaden the positional tails.

The resulting win probabilities are led by **Antonelli (37.89%)**, **Norris (34.51%)**, **Verstappen (11.38%)**, **Hamilton (6.27%)**, **Russell (4.34%)**, **Leclerc (3.03%)** and **Piastri (1.47%)**. Norris has the track-position advantage; Antonelli gets a narrow overall edge from Mercedes' high-fuel evidence and season-long strength.

Retirement risk is above a normal dry-race baseline because the circuit is wall-lined and unfamiliar, practice produced several heavy crashes, support racing produced a first-lap pile-up, and 2026 reliability has been poor. Stroll is the largest individual risk after repeated Honda failures and this weekend's fresh-PU water-pressure problem; Bearman also carries extra DNS/retirement risk while Haas rebuilds the car after his FP3 impact. The model averages about **4.82 race retirements**.

`retirement` is modeled separately from classification. A driver retiring late can still receive a numbered FIA classification; earlier retirements go to `nc`. `dns` includes failure to take the start, while `dsq` is a small separate post-event risk.

H1 Antonelli clinches victory over Verstappen and Norris in Spanish GP
P Kimi Antonelli achieved his eighth Grand Prix win of the 2026 season to further increase his advantage in the Drivers’ Championship.
P Kimi Antonelli has boosted his title ambitions with victory in the Spanish Grand Prix, the Mercedes driver edging out Red Bull’s Max Verstappen and McLaren’s Lando Norris in a race swayed by strategy.
P The opening laps saw plenty of clashes up and down the field, with Norris narrowly holding onto the lead from pole position as Antonelli cut two corners during his concerted efforts to pass the Briton.
P Antonelli ultimately didn’t need to overtake him on track thanks to a Virtual Safety Car, which played perfectly into Mercedes’ hands but ruined Norris’ chances for victory. A tale of contrasting pit stops unfolded as the Italian gained the net race lead while a slow change dropped Norris behind both Antonelli and Verstappen.
P Despite expressing worries with his steering, the 20-year-old inherited control of the race once Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, who didn’t box during the VSC, gave up on his hopes for a Safety Car and finally peeled into the pits after 48 laps.
P Adding an eighth win to his season tally, Antonelli has extended his lead to 81 points in the Drivers’ Championship as his team mate George Russell settled for P5, and Lewis Hamilton retired early on due to a issue with his brakes.
P Race results
P FORMULA 1 TAG HEUER GRAN PREMIO DE ESPAÑA 2026
P Liam Lawson was sixth in the second Red Bull ahead of Franco Colapinto, who made it a successful day for Alpine as their sole scorer, McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg.
P Haas’ Esteban Ocon just missed out on points in P11 and was followed by Pierre Gasly and Gabriel Bortoleto, while Yuki Tsunoda took P14 in his third weekend competing for Racing Bulls.
P Alex Albon was up next as the lone finisher for Williams, leading Ollie Bearman, local favourite Fernando Alonso and Cadillac’s Valtteri Bottas.
P There were four retirements in total – Carlos Sainz failed to complete his home race, Sergio Perez faced a suspected water system issue, and Lance Stroll joined Hamilton in his brake troubles.
H3 AS IT HAPPENED
P The Madring had already delivered some of the drama many have come to expect with the debut of a new circuit – Lindblad, Hamilton and Bearman endured shunts across FP2 and FP3, although all bar the Haas man were able to partake in Qualifying.
P Hamilton managed to bounce back and claim provisional pole but was quickly outpaced by Antonelli, before McLaren’s Norris completed what he thought was “one of the best laps” of his career to snatch the top spot in style.
P Verstappen took a respectable third for Red Bull to lead both Ferrari drivers and the second Mercedes of Russell, who admitted after Qualifying that problems with overheating tyres had limited his performance over the weekend.
P He wasn’t the only one concerned about the Pirelli rubber, as previous sessions had shown that graining and thermal degradation could play a significant role in Sunday’s Grand Prix.
P As the race start approached at 1500 local time, Haas confirmed that Bearman would start from the pit lane with a new chassis and power unit elements installed following his crash.
P Additionally, Stroll and Sainz had grid penalties imposed after Aston Martin fitted engine components to the Canadian’s car to relegate him to P21, just behind Sainz. The stewards concluded that the Williams driver had impeded Cadillac’s Bottas in Q1, dropping him from P17 to P20.
P It was revealed that the teams had opted for a wide range of tyre strategies – the front-row starters were on the medium compound, as were Colapinto and Lindblad at the tail end of the top 10.
P Verstappen and Hamilton went for the bold option of softs in the hope of making up positions on the opening lap, while Leclerc, Russell, Piastri and Lawson focused on the long game with the white-walled hard tyres.
P They were joined by Bortoleto, Gasly, Tsunoda, Alonso, Bottas, Sainz, Stroll and Bearman, whereas Ocon, Albon and Perez chose the mediums. Audi’s Hulkenberg was the only other driver on softs, seemingly targeting an immediate improvement into the points.
P As the five red lights went out for the Madring’s inaugural Grand Prix, polesitter Norris came under instant pressure from Antonelli, who took the inside line but was forced to bail out and cut the first chicane. That allowed the McLaren driver to just about cling onto the lead while Antonelli stuck close by.
P As another attack followed, the Italian made a near-identical error and went off track once again, giving Verstappen the opportunity to execute a clean overtake at the Bunker to surge into P2.
P However, Hamilton wasn’t happy with how the Red Bull driver had stayed ahead at the first corner, insisting that the position needed to be given back. Verstappen, almost simultaneously, reported that Hamilton “almost shunted into me” and was “out of control”, but his complaints didn’t have the intended effect.
P His race engineer instructed him to give the spot to Hamilton in order to avoid a possible penalty, and despite a small argument from the Dutchman’s side, he obeyed the order and subsequently let both Antonelli and the Briton through.
P To Hamilton’s frustration, the switch didn’t last for long amid his own struggles with the brakes, and he dropped back behind Verstappen and his Ferrari team mate Leclerc. The issue rapidly worsened and he could only watch as his rivals charged past, with the Scuderia deciding to retire the car just seven laps in.
P With Hamilton out of contention, Norris had steadily built his lead to 4.5s over Antonelli, aided by the Italian suffering an off-track moment that cost him a chunk of time. The closest battle at this stage was between Colapinto and Lawson for P6, both drivers having fought past McLaren’s Piastri when the Australian made contact with Russell on the opening lap.
P Elsewhere, Russell had clearly spent some time revising his tyre management overnight, suggesting to the team that they could try an alternative strategy to get past Leclerc, who was running in P4 just ahead of the Briton.
P A check-in on the grid’s two Spaniards showed that their home crowd had little to celebrate – not only was a top-10 finish a distant prospect, but they also came to blows at Turn 5, with Alonso adamant that Sainz had squeezed him into the wall. The stewards agreed with his view, later handing the Williams driver a five-second penalty for the collision.
P Meanwhile, Norris’ advantage at the front continued to increase, and he received further encouragement when the team informed him that Antonelli’s medium tyres weren’t coping with the high-grip asphalt as well as his, implying that he might try to extend his opening stint.
P That approach soon fell apart when Aston Martin’s Stroll came to a halt at Turn 20, marking the second retirement of the day caused by brake problems. The Virtual Safety Car was deployed, handing Mercedes and Red Bull the perfect opportunity to call Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen into the pits.
P The mandatory reduced speeds only lasted as long as it took to bring Stroll’s car behind the barrier, meaning that Norris ran out of time to take advantage and only stopped once normal racing conditions resumed.
P Adding insult to injury, it was an agonisingly slow tyre change that kept him stationary for 7s and he eventually emerged in P5 behind Leclerc – who hadn’t pitted – Antonelli, Verstappen and Russell.
P With the sole Ferrari driver now leading, Antonelli initially closed the gap before falling further back, stating that “the steering wheel feels weird”. Mercedes couldn’t find any reason why in their data, but did warn him that any further track limit violations could result in a time penalty.
P Over half the race distance down, Norris was giving it his all to recover from the disastrous timing of the Virtual Safety Car as he battled to get past Russell, which was made much easier when the latter was brought in for a second stop.

P Lewis Hamilton's head-on crash in the final hour of practice gave his mechanics a hefty repair job in order to make Qualifying, but that didn’t seem to dissuade the seven-time World Champion, as he went on to claim provisional pole with the first Q3 flying laps.
P Ending up fourth in the final reckoning, directly ahead of team mate Charles Leclerc, there was still a possibility that a podium was on the cards, especially when Hamilton got a superb launch off the line.
P Verstappen, who Hamilton had jumped, cut the chicane before eventually allowing the Ferrari driver back ahead, only for Hamilton to suffer a brake problem that sent him through several run-off areas and eventually forced his retirement.
P It was a better day for Leclerc, who was likely left questioning what could have been had Ferrari’s hope of a Safety Car or red flag come to fruition. He did not pit under the VSC and thereby inherited the lead, but the lack of any further incidents left him with no choice but to finally pit after 48 laps on the hard tyres.
P The gaps that had opened up between the frontrunners and the rest of the top 10 helped the Monegasque to come back out in P4, where he held off Mercedes’ Russell to bring home a respectable haul of points.
H3 Best of the rest for Verstappen after giving positions up
P Max Verstappen claimed P2 in Madrid, despite begrudgingly giving back places in the opening laps after tangling with Lewis Hamilton.
P The Ferrari driver got ahead after lights out, with Verstappen cutting the first turn by driving off track to keep his P3 starting position.
P The Dutchman said on the radio that Hamilton “almost shunted me”, and tried to resist Red Bull's instructions to give the place back to avoid a potential penalty, especially after he had since overtaken Antonelli for P2.
P After giving in and allowing both Antonelli and Hamilton through, he quickly returned to the podium places after the Ferrari driver had a problem with his brakes.
P Verstappen was also able to make the most of the VSC to limit positions lost during his pit stop, and eventually held off a charging Norris in the closing laps.
H3 Ugochukwu takes F3 title in Madrid
P Both F2 and F3 championships were in action at the Madring, with the latter concluding their season in the Spanish city.
P Ugo Ugochukwu was up against Freddie Slater for the title, and it was the Campos Racing man who took the crown courtesy of a P2 finish in the final Feature Race.
P Slater’s chances were dealt a blow when he was unable to score in the Sprint Race, before failing to finish the first Feature Race, meaning the pair entered the final race tied on points.
P Eighth in the second Feature Race was not enough to deny his rival, Ugochukwu taking the title by 14 points in the end, with Tuukka Taponen also left celebrating after taking a maiden F3 victory on Sunday.
P Over in F2, Dino Beganovic took a lights-to-flag victory in the Feature Race for DAMS Lucas Oil, as he led home Rodin Motorsport’s Alexander Dunne and Hitech’s Ritomo Miyata.
P Championship leader Nikola Tsolov finished down the order, but his rival Rafael Camara could not capitalise, coming home P10 after a penalty to only narrowly reduce his deficit in the standings.
P Tsolov leads by seven points, with those two set to resume their rivalry next time out in Baku.
H3 Football stars out in force while Madrid welcomes tennis royalty to the paddock
P There were plenty of famous faces from the world of sport on the Madring grid on Sunday, with Real Madrid giving a few players the day off to come and watch F1.
P Their manager Jose Mourinho was also on the grid, and having beaten Rayo Vallecano 4-1 in La Liga action the previous evening, he was in an understandably good mood. As was Jude Bellingham, who scored in that match before using his Sunday off to catch up with some of his countrymen.
P Vinicius Jnr was seen laughing and joking with Gabriel Bortoleto, while Real Madrid’s goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois towered over some of the drivers – at six foot seven, he is considerably taller than even the likes of Russell and Esteban Ocon.
P Footballing legends David Beckham, Zinedine Zidane and Roberto Carlos were also in attendance, as was retired tennis star Rafael Nadal, who was spotted down at Ferrari.

H1 ‘The potential is there’ – Why Vasseur believes Ferrari had the pace to win in Madrid
P Fred Vasseur has given his thoughts on Ferrari’s performance in the Spanish Grand Prix, which saw Charles Leclerc finish P4 after Lewis Hamilton retired.
P Fred Vasseur was confident that Charles Leclerc could’ve won the Spanish Grand Prix if an incident had disrupted the latter stages of the race, with the Ferrari Team Principal believing that “the potential is there” for the team.
P Leclerc qualified fifth and gained an early position from the retirement of his team mate Lewis Hamilton, but unlike those around him, he and the team opted not to pit for fresh tyres when the Virtual Safety Car was deployed.
P As a result, he inherited the lead and maintained a consistent gap to Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli, with Ferrari hoping that the race would see a red flag or Safety Car to give Leclerc what would essentially be a free pit stop.
P Unfortunately, that didn’t materialise and he was finally called in after spending nearly 50 laps on the hard compound, dropping him out of podium contention. He eventually crossed the line 29.116s behind Antonelli and narrowly held off George Russell for P4.
P “You see that you always have positives and negatives, it doesn't matter the weekend,” Vasseur said. “The pace of Charles in the race was more than good – we did a stint of 49 laps I think with the hard and the pace was still there.
P “All the teams did the same with one car on softs or mediums and another one on hards to cover all the options. He was leading the group of [drivers on] hards and I think with a second incident, a red flag, it was the win.
P “A Safety Car, it would have been P2, P3. It's more a strategy than something else and on his side, the pace was good. It's the only thing that we can do on Sunday. If we missed something, it's more yesterday [in Qualifying]. Today I think we did what we had to do – we took the risks we had to take and the pace is the pace that we need to have.”
P While Leclerc was able to demonstrate Ferrari’s strength in race trim, Hamilton only lasted a short time before a brake issue forced him to retire the car, marking his first DNF of the season.
P The Briton enjoyed a fantastic launch to instantly challenge Max Verstappen for P3, with the Dutchman offering him the position after he cut the first corner. However, Hamilton quickly began to drop back as he reported that the brake pedal was going long and he couldn’t stop the car.
P He did manage to make it safely back to the garage, where he was left to rue the missed opportunity, telling Sky Sports F1: “I think we had the car to fight for a win today, and unfortunately it just didn't work out.”
P Asked whether the problem was caused by a small brush with the wall, Vasseur replied: “Obviously I don't know, because they were working on the car when I left. The pedal was long on the end of Lap 1, I think, and we tried to fix it from the pit wall, and then it happened again a couple of corners later, and at this kind of track it makes no sense to take a crazy risk.
P “There were still 56 [laps to go]. The first time it happened was from Lap 2 and it was too risky.”

H1 What the teams said – Race day in Spain
P The drivers and teams report back on all the action from the Madring for the Spanish Grand Prix.
H3 Mercedes
P Kimi Antonelli got a great start from P2, but when challenging for the lead cut the apex of the corner and was forced to cede position. His attempts to do so were messy and he briefly fell behind Verstappen until the Dutchman had to do the same thing. That left Antonelli second, a few seconds behind race leader Norris. But when the Italian got a cheap pit stop under the VSC, he became the de facto leader and from there he kept his race pretty clean to take his eighth win of the year.
P As for George Russell, he had contact with Piastri at the start but was lucky to hold on to P6. The team opted to pit him under the VSC too, even though he started on the hards, and then did not think the mediums would last so pitted Russell a second time. That dropped him back again, and he finished fifth.
P Kimi Antonelli, 1st
P "It was great to get the victory today, but we know we were a little bit fortunate with the timing of the Virtual Safety Car. Lando (Norris) was in control at the front, but we were able to dive into the pits just as the Virtual Safety Car was deployed, make the cheap stop onto the Hard, get the net lead and run to the end. We probably didn’t deserve to win therefore but we will of course take it.
P "We can also be happy with our pace today. We know we are still out of step with other teams in terms of upgrades, but we have been able to win the last two races at very different circuits. That is encouraging as we continue the season; we have a good position in the championships but we know there is still a very long way to go."
P George Russell, 5th
P "No matter what we had done with strategy today we would have finished P5. The Virtual Safety Car came at the worst point for everyone who had started on the Hard tyre like me, and the best point for those who had started on the Medium. Unfortunately, that is how racing goes sometimes but it is a little bit the story of my season so far! It was very difficult to overtake today but I’ve enjoyed driving the Madring overall this weekend.
P "It is going to be an intense run to the end of the season. I’m looking forward to getting back to the factory, working with the team, and getting ready for the first of three triple-headers. My pace today, particularly on the Hard tyre, felt good so we can be encouraged by that as we head to Baku."
P Toto Wolff, Head of Mercedes-Benz Motorsport
P "We are pleased to have taken the first victory at the Madring; it has been another successful new event for F1 at a great location. Kimi drove well and, whilst the Virtual Safety Car played into his hands, he drove well to bring the car home at what has proved to be a very challenging circuit. To take another win at such a different track to Monza, having not brought a major update package to the car since Canada, is very encouraging.
P "On George’s side, he was slightly unfortunate with the timing of the Virtual Safety Car. We started him on the Hard tyre, intending to go long, but we had to take the cheap stop under the Virtual Safety Car and to do something different if we were to try and beat Leclerc. The Ferrari stayed out and we switch George to the Medium but unfortunately it wasn’t the strongest tyre today. George reported early on that he was suffering so we went back to the Hard compound; ultimately whatever we had done we would have come home P5 today.
P "We now have one week to get ready for Baku and the beginning of the first of three triple-headers. Extending our lead in the championships is good but we know there is still so much racing to come. It is going to be an intense run to the end of the season but we’re excited for that challenge."
P Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director
P "That was a great result for Kimi and a really strong weekend for the team. We clearly benefited from the timing of the Virtual Safety Car, but credit goes to the drivers and everyone in the garage for being ready to react. The execution of both stops was excellent and that helped us take the win today.
P "For Kimi, the decision to pit under the Virtual Safety Car was the one that ultimately put him in the net lead of the race. George's situation was a little more complicated. We had elected to do the opposite of Leclerc strategically because, when you're behind, you often need to try something different to create an opportunity. As the race unfolded, though, it became clear that the Hard tyre was performing better than we had expected and was the compound to be on. That said, if we had mirrored the Ferrari’s strategy, we would have still likely finished P5 with overtaking proving so difficult.
P "Ultimately, the Virtual Safety Car arrived at the perfect moment for the cars that could switch onto the Hard tyre, and that's sometimes how racing goes. The important thing is that we've come away with a race win, a strong points haul, and strengthened our position in both championships.
P "We'll regroup over the next few days and prepare for the run to the finish of the season. Nine races in 11 weeks is going to be a demanding stretch for everyone, but we've put ourselves in a good position in both title fights and we'll keep pushing right to the final Grand Prix."
H3 Red Bull
P Max Verstappen cut the corner at Turn 2 when fighting with Hamilton, and was even briefly ahead of Antonelli. But the team told him to give the positions back, which after Hamilton retired left him third. The Dutchman benefitted from a VSC pit stop to jump ahead of Norris, and managed to catch Antonelli to show the RB22 had some good race pace. He kept a charging Norris at bay in the closing stages for his second straight rostrum.
P As for Liam Lawson, he ran a long stint on the hards, and had to fight hard to come home sixth. He could not keep a fresher shod Russell at bay, but did manage to overtake Gasly before a lonely end to his race.
P Max Verstappen, 2nd
P “It was a great result, and we really maximised our performance, with finishing P2 on this track a solid way to wrap up a good weekend. At the start, Lewis clipped the kerb and jumped back onto the racing line, I had to go off track, otherwise both of us would have taken damage. I don't think we had the pace to challenge for the lead anyway, Kimi and Lando were faster than me throughout, so I'm happy with second. It's a circuit that's very difficult to pass on; if you position yourself in the middle, there isn't really a way through, so I was able to hold off Lando until the end. This double header has been a positive one. The car has been in a decent window both weekends, and we've been able to score consistently good points over the last few races. A podium is a nice way to end the European swing."
P Liam Lawson, 6th
P "I think it was a decent race. We had good speed through parts of it, but I just think we weren’t on the ideal strategy today. We went for the alternate strategy, starting on the Hards. At the start I lost the position to Franco and lost a lot of time as it was, but by the time I cleared him the VSC came out and they’d boxed, so it was just tricky from there. The start was exciting and I had to take a lot of risks to get the move done on Franco because it’s quite difficult to overtake here. It would’ve been nice to start a bit higher, but considering where we did start, the result today was good and I’m happy we managed to gain two places in the Race. I’m much more confident in the car this week, we’ve made a couple of great steps, so there are some good things to take away from the weekend."
P Laurent Mekies, Team Principal
P “After Monza another strong result from the whole Team at the end of a tough race. Once again, Max extracted absolutely everything from the car, as he always does. There was obviously some frustration at the start when he had to give the place back to Lewis, but the Team on the pit wall took a good look at it and, credit to them, made the difficult call. It was painful at the time, but Max immediately got himself back into the fight and was outstanding all the way to the flag, including a great defence against the McLaren in the final laps.
P "It was also a strong race and some good points from Liam. It certainly wasn’t easy towards the end of his first stint on worn Hard tyres, but he kept his cool and showed good pace in the final stint.
P "Max’s P2 is his fifth podium in the last seven races and, although we have had a couple of tricky moments along the way, we are continuing to close the gap and credit needs to go to everyone working behind the scenes at Milton Keynes, improving every aspect of the car and its PU.”
H3 McLaren
P Lando Norris had a great start from pole and after some early shenanigans with track limits, settled into the lead. He built a decent gap to Antonelli behind but when a VSC was called he was already past the pit lane entry. As such, Antonelli and Verstappen behind pitted for a cheap stop. By the time Norris came around, the VSC had ended – and then he had a slow pit stop to boot, which dropped him down the order.
P The reigning World Champion did well to fight back to the podium, but luck was not on his side today. Nor was it on Oscar Piastri’s, who suffered front wing damage after being squeezed by Russell off the line. That dropped him out of the top 10, but he ran a long first stint to fight back, and pulled off some overtakes to at least finish in the points.
P Lando Norris, 3rd
P “I feel like I drove a perfect race today, my tyre management was very strong, and I felt a step ahead of everyone. Qualifying was perfect, the race in terms of performance was perfect, and we were quickest by a big margin. It's just incredibly frustrating to lose in a way that has nothing to do with performance. I was the only driver on the whole grid who didn't get a pit stop under the VSC, and I lost around twenty seconds of race time because of it.
P “There are still positives to take from this weekend in terms of what we can do. The pace on Sunday is clearly there, we were better than everyone today, and that's reassuring. Saturday is still an area we need to improve, but if we can close that gap and avoid situations like today, we win. We'll take today on the chin, keep pushing, and go again.”
P Oscar Piastri, 8th
P “It was a tough one for us today, and a pretty painful race from start to finish. I got squeezed by Russell which then broke my front wing on the first lap, and from there we just got stuck in traffic, which is tricky with the lack of overtaking here. Unfortunately, the VSC timing wasn't ideal for the Hard tyre starters like myself. When we did pit, the Mediums didn't perform how we wanted them to, and I was back in traffic.
P “The positive we can take is that there are some good learnings, especially on how to get the most out of the car. We also had some decent pace on the Hard tyre in clean air, which is always encouraging. We will review, see what more we can learn and then and take it into the next part of the season.”
P Andrea Stella, Team Principal
P “Today is a day of mixed emotions, but we leave with our heads held high and a smile on our faces. Lando was the fastest driver on track and absolutely deserved the victory. The pace we showed was phenomenal, especially at a circuit where we didn't expect to be so strong. Unfortunately, factors entirely outside our control, specifically the timing of the Virtual Safety Car, meant the win was taken from us. We reviewed all options, but the circumstances left us with no viable alternative strategy. It's frustrating when you have the performance to win and the racing gods aren't on your side, but we will take it on the chin.
P “The biggest positive is the clear evidence that our car is competitive and capable of fighting at the front. The team did an exceptional job all weekend to unlock this level of performance, and it gives us great confidence for the upcoming races. We are closing the gap in the championship and have proven we can be a threat on Sundays. While it was a tougher day for Oscar, who was compromised by damage at the start, we are working hard with him to unlock his full potential. We look forward to Baku, ready to fight for podiums and victories.”
H3 Ferrari
P Lewis Hamilton was fighting with Verstappen at the start, but his race unravelled soon after when a brake issue forced him to pit to retire the car, his first DNF of the season. That left Charles Leclerc to fly the flag for Ferrari, which he did in style. On the hard tyre, he ran an exceptionally long opening stint to lead the race for much of the afternoon. But with no more disruptions, he eventually did have to pit under normal race conditions, which dropped him to fourth.
P Lewis Hamilton, DNF
P "Firstly, a big thank you to the team for the job they did throughout the weekend. We were in a position to fight for a strong result and the car had been performing well.
P "Unfortunately, we encountered an issue with the braking system very quickly into the race which brought our afternoon to an early end. It’s disappointing, especially considering all the effort that went into the weekend both here at the track and back at the factory. We will turn our attention to the next race and do our best to come back strong there."
P Charles Leclerc, 4th
P "The race was good and we brought home what was realistically the best result possible, given that this track is so difficult to overtake on. We did a good job with the strategy, playing our cards to suit our situation. We decided to take our chance and wait for a Safety Car to come up before the end of the race to gain an advantage, but it didn’t play out that way in the end. If we had been on the opposite strategy, I would have finished fourth as well, so either way, we extracted the most we could out of our race.
P "Now we take a break and reset ahead of the next round in Baku, a track I’ve always enjoyed racing on in the past."
P Fred Vasseur, Team Principal
P "Like a few other teams, we split the strategy today, starting one car on the Soft compound and the other on the Hard. With Charles, we were leading the group that started on the Hard tyre and he drove a very strong first stint, pushing for almost 50 laps while maintaining good pace throughout.
P "We knew there was a reasonable chance of a Safety Car or a red flag, so we decided to extend the stint and keep that opportunity open. A red flag could have put us in a position to fight for the win, while a late Safety Car could have given us a shot at third. In the end neither happened, but I think it was absolutely worth trying and Charles delivered a very solid performance. As for Lewis, at this stage we don’t yet know the exact cause of the brake system issue that forced him to retire and we will investigate it thoroughly. Regarding the championship, our approach remains the same: we take it one race at a time, and our focus now turns to Baku."
H3 Alpine
P Franco Colapinto made a great start to pick up a couple of places and run solidly in the top 10. He pitted under the VSC which dropped him back, but the Argentinian racer was happy to bide his time and work his way back up the order. His team mate ran the longest first stint of anyone on the hard tyres, eventually pitting on the penultimate lap. Pierre Gasly had hung it out in the hopes of a Safety Car, but that stop dropped him out of the points and he was handed a five-second penalty for speeding in the pit lane too.
P Pierre Gasly, 12th
P “We gave it absolutely everything we could today but, unfortunately, circumstances did not play into our hands. Yesterday we did not maximise Qualifying and that really left us out of position on the grid and gave us an uphill battle to score points. We had to try something and took some risks. We were fast throughout the race, I left nothing out there, but we just needed a VSC or a SC to benefit at the end. Like for others, that didn't happen, so I'm left a bit frustrated but still pleased the team managed to score important points. We'll debrief on many things from the weekend and continue putting our efforts into making the car faster and more complete at every event.”
P Franco Colapinto, 7th
P “I'm very happy with the end result today with P7 and scoring six points for the team, especially as this track layout probably does not best suit the strengths of our package too well. I had a very good race start again today and I managed the tyres well and then kept the position. The VSC came and we did our pit-stop to save time, like some others around us. The second stint lasted until the end of the race, so it was very long and took some defending throughout. I caught up to Gabriel [Bortoleto] but I lost a lot of time even if it probably did not mean we'd have finished in a position higher. I'm pleased to score points today and be in front of our direct competitors as we continue to close the gap in the Championship. It's probably my best race weekend in terms of execution this year, I maximised everything in Qualifying and did what I had to do today. We will all debrief as a team and continue to develop the car and maximise our performances each weekend.”
P Flavio Briatore, Executive Advisor
P “The aim heading into the weekend was to be ahead of Racing Bulls and close the gap to them in the Constructors' Championship. We did that, so we can be pleased with the result from today's race. Franco did a mega job all weekend and scored six valuable points for the team. With Pierre's race, given where he qualified and started the race, the only option we had to score points was to keep him out and hopefully benefit from a late Safety Car. As did other teams around us. Also, fantastic job to Formula One and the organisers to put on this amazing new race event in Madrid, which I am sure will only grow and get better.”
H3 Racing Bulls
P Arvid Lindblad was running in the points in the opening stages, dropping out after pitting under the VSC. From there he was patient, picking up places as others eventually pitted. He lost out to Piastri, but kept ahead of Hulkenberg as he scored yet again for the team.
P Yuki Tsunoda had a very eventual race, starting with contact at the start courtesy of Sainz’s Williams. He also had a moment with Perez, but could not make much headway and came home outside the points.
P Arvid Lindblad, 9th
P "I'm pleased to come away from a challenging weekend with a couple more points. Approaching the race, we knew strategy was going to be really important, but once the VSC came out, almost everyone pitted, so there wasn't much more to play with. From there, I just pushed pretty much flat out for the rest of the race on the Hard tyre. We had good pace throughout and for most of the race we were right behind Franco. I tried everything I could, being smart with my energy management and using it differently to see if I could find a way through. Unfortunately, there just wasn't a real opportunity to overtake. It wasn't the most exciting race, but I think we can be satisfied with how we handled the weekend following the setback on Friday."
P Yuki Tsunoda, 14th
P "Today wasn’t easy at all. The race was almost over for me at Turn 1, where I picked up a lot of damage from the collision with Sainz, and the impact that had on our pace was significant. Considering the damage, I don’t think the pace was too bad, but I lost a few positions at the start. With overtaking being so difficult around here, there wasn’t much opportunity to recover them. I gave it everything I had and really enjoyed being back in the car again. A big thank you to the team for another opportunity this weekend.”
P Alan Permane, Team Principal
P "We had a pretty decent day today with Arvid coming away with some points, so can feel confident that the pace is there. Yuki's race was compromised on Lap 1 when Carlos Sainz collided with him and caused damage to the car. This cost him at least half a second and led to a tough race overall. It's a great circuit here in Madrid, and I think it will continue to grow in popularity over the years. We look forward to heading to Baku in a couple of weeks as we kick off the triple header."
H3 Audi
P Audi managed to get one car home in the points after running different strategies out there. Nico Hulkenberg started on the softs, and pitted under the VSC which made his race. He climbed to P10, for his third score of the year. Gabriel Bortoleto started on the hards and hung it out in the hopes of a Safety Car. That never came, and he dropped out of the top 10 after eventually pitting, the Brazilian also handed a warning for moving under braking.
P Nico Hulkenberg, 10th
P "We got the maximum out of what we had today. Starting on the soft tyre meant the early Virtual Safety Car was the right window for us to pit, and the pit crew did a fantastic job to get me ahead of Esteban [Ocon]. That was probably the key moment of our race because it gave us the track position we needed. From there, it was all about managing the tyres. Overtaking was very difficult with everyone running at a similar pace, so there wasn't much room to make further progress. We've been towards the top of this midfield fight for a while now, hopefully we will soon make the extra step we need to keep moving forward."
P Gabriel Bortoleto, 13th
P “We got unlucky with the Virtual Safety Car today, which pretty much messed up with our plans, and after that nothing else happened until the end of the race - not much more we could have done from there, especially as chances to overtake were slim.
P “Overall, it's been a weekend of learnings. It wasn’t the best, but it was not all that bad either, and I have quite enjoyed racing around here. In qualifying, we were close to making it into Q3 again, and that was more or less where our pace has been all weekend. Now, a week to recharge and get back to work before we head to Baku in two weeks.”
P Allan McNish, Racing Director
P “Overall, we’re happy to have gained a point. It was always going to be a difficult race from a strategy point of view, with overtaking being very difficult and it looking strongly like a one-stop race. We dropped positions again at the start, which is an area we know is one of our weaknesses, but from there I was very pleased with how we worked as a team.
P “We played a real team game today. Nico switched from the soft onto the hard tyre, while we ran an alternative strategy with Gabi which covered pretty much every scenario. Gabi did a great job to run very long on the hard, with the hope that a Safety Car, Virtual Safety Car or red flag later in the race could give him a significant tyre advantage, or a free stop, and propel him back into the points. On the other side, Nico was very strong on both the soft and the hard and came very close to getting ahead of Lindblad at the end.
P “Ultimately, I have to say the point today was delivered by the team in the pits. Nico came in behind Ocon and went out ahead of him after a fantastically quick stop, and the team repeated that performance when Gabi came in. It was a very good team effort, strategically, in the pits and from both drivers. It’s another point for us, and now we look forward to Baku.”
H3 Haas
P Ollie Bearman took on some PU components and thus started from the pit lane, which meant a long day for him down the order. But at least he has plenty of engine parts in his pool now for the rest of the season. Ocon started on the mediums and got away well to pick up some places. He was able to pit under the VSC and was right in the mix for the final point, but ran out of time to chase up to the Audi of Hulkenberg.
P Oliver Bearman, 16th
P “Unfortunately, the VSC came at a bad time and I didn’t benefit from it at all – but it’s been a tough weekend, and I only have myself to blame for that. On a positive, this weekend has taught me a lot, maybe more so than a clean, easy, straightforward weekend, as I took a lot from yesterday and won’t repeat that mistake. The car was strong, so whenever I was in clear air, I was right on the pace with our competition, it was just unfortunate that it was rare that I had free air as I was stuck in traffic. That gives me a good outlook heading to Baku, so now we can turn the page, reset and come back stronger.”
P Esteban Ocon, 11th
P “We’re disappointed as we deserve much more, we deserved to be in the points today. The plan was to get both Audis at the start, and we managed to do so, and we knew it would be hard to hold them, but we did so until the stop. At the stop, we lost the position, so we need to see what I could’ve done better, if I could’ve stopped in a better position or what, as I thought it was a decent stop but they must’ve had a better one. We gave it our all out there and I’m proud of everyone, as we came from being out in Q1 and now we’re fighting for points, so it’s positive and encouraging for the rest of the races.”
P Ayao Komatsu, Team Principal
P “We’re all very disappointed to finish P11, but I think it’s really good that we’re back in the position that we’re all a bit disappointed by that. The car was functioning very well, the drivers drove well, trackside and remote operations were really good, I think we did our best today. We lost out on the pit stop against Audi, but I don’t believe it was our team’s fault, it’s really the equipment that we need to improve to give them a better chance. I’m honestly very happy, it was a huge team effort all around, and the car’s consistency was there, no issues as we’ve had previously, so we need to learn from it. I’m sure Ollie will also come back strong, so it’s been a positive weekend.”
H3 Williams
P Carlos Sainz had a home race to forget in Madrid. He made contact with Tsunoda at the start after locking up, in what the stewards called a racing incident. He made more contact with his countryman Alonso midway through, the Aston Martin man’s ire evident over the radio. That one earned Sainz a time penalty. He pitted to serve that, was warned about track limits and wound up retiring with car damage. Alex Albon had a quieter race, but lacked the speed to climb up the order.
P Carlos Sainz, DNF
P “It’s been a tougher weekend in Madrid than what I would have liked. I had a very strong start, picking up positions off the line, but I went deep into turn 1 and had contact with Yuki. From there on, the damage to the floor meant I was lacking a lot of downforce and couldn’t keep it on track for the remainder of the race, forcing us to retire. Regarding the penalty, two cars don’t fit into that corner so being ahead, there was little I could do. It’s a disappointing way to end the first race here, but ultimately, scoring points was always going to be near impossible for us.
P “The fans have been absolutely amazing from start to finish and I’ve felt their support all weekend. The track is great and for the first year I think it’s been a great event overall. There needs to be some work done to create better overtaking opportunities.
P “Looking ahead to Baku, I’m hopeful that the upgrades will put us more in the mix with the cars ahead and that we can come back stronger.”
P Alex Albon, 15th
P “It was a tricky race and a difficult weekend for us, but I think that was probably the best we could've hoped for today. Beating both Astons and one of the Haas' is what we could realistically maximise, so that was our accomplishment for the day - we're still too far behind to be properly competing with the midfield, and it was pretty tough out there.
P "We've got the upgrade coming in Baku, so hopefully that moves us up relative to the midfield and at least gets us into that fight. Realistically it's probably not big enough to shift us forward completely, but our priority unfortunately has shifted to next year. The midfield teams have brought more upgrades than usual this season and the development race is moving so fast, which is something we are focused on improving.”
P James Vowles, Team Principal
P “A very tricky day – we don't have pace here this weekend. Fortunately, we have a small step coming for Baku, but it's still going to be a difficult run to the end of the year. It was fantastic to see the support for Carlos, the entire grandstand was cheering him on all the way through the weekend. That level of support is what we need to keep us going in the tough times. Well done to Alex, he performed well all weekend and that was the best the car could achieve today. Onwards and upwards.”
H3 Aston Martin
P Lance Stroll caused the pivotal Virtual Safety Car when he parked up in the run off area with a car problem. He made it to a gap in the barriers, so the marshals were able to push his car out the way quickly – something that ultimately cost Norris. As for Fernando Alonso, he got his elbows out and fought hard at his second home race of the season, especially against Sainz’s Williams. Alonso was frustrated with their moment, feeling he had been squeezed and the stewards agreed, handing his rival a penalty.
P Fernando Alonso, 17th
P "We needed a chaotic race today to try and change our situation and in the end we didn’t have much to fight for. But we tried different things and keep learning about the updated package. Unfortunately, Carlos [Sainz] hit me and it meant we had to pit to replace the front wing. There was a penalty given out so that’s the decision taken by the FIA and I think it was correct. It was incredible to see the support of the fans today and I really enjoyed the atmosphere.”
P Lance Stroll, DNF
P “I picked up quite a bit of damage in the opening laps. We tried to keep going, but then I started having some brake issues and the pedal was getting very long, so I locked up. I tried to spin the car around in the run-off, but I didn’t have enough power, so unfortunately that was the end of the race. It’s been a difficult weekend in Madrid.”
P Adrian Newey, Team Principal
P “A disappointing afternoon for us in Madrid. With Lance retiring early with damage and Fernando also suffering damage after contact with Carlos Sainz, we could not show our true pace. Fernando drove a solid race in front of the Spanish fans which helped to gather useful data on this new car for us to analyse. We now focus on Baku where we will bring further weight saving measures and continue to optimise the package.”
H3 Cadillac
P It was not to be for Sergio Perez, who was fighting with a gaggle of cars but was forced to retire with a suspected water systems issue. That left Valtteri Bottas to bring home more valuable data for Cadillac, although the Finn finished well back from Alonso ahead. Cadillac will hope to show some improvements in the next triple header, before they head for home soil later in the year.
P Sergio Perez, DNF
P “Our race was going really strong up until the moment we suffered with a suspected water system issue. I think it's been one of the strongest weekends we've had as a team so far, pushing everything to the limit. We raced all the cars around us, keeping Yuki [Tsunoda] behind before we stopped and fought with the Williams all the way through, staying within a second of [Alex] Albon, so we can be happy with how our race was going.”
P Valtteri Bottas, 18th
P “Sadly not much action for me today. I was hoping for a few more things to happen but we knew that the pace here would be difficult and it was a tough race. The brake temperatures were an issue we had to manage quite a lot throughout, and the nature of this track highlights a lot of the issues that we have, but we know where we need to improve and we will keep working on it.”
P Marcin Budkowski, Team Principal
P “Thanks to Valtteri who brought the car to the finish while managing a few issues during the race. We opted for a strategy aimed at maximising race disruptions but it didn’t quite pay off. Checo had a great first lap, gaining several positions and was racing against the Williams and the Racing Bulls before we had to retire the car with a Power Unit issue. We’re looking forward to a busy week of preparation back at the factory before our next street race in Baku.”
H3 Pirelli
P Dario Marrafuschi, Pirelli Motorsport Director
P “The teams approached today's race differently from what had been simulated on track on Friday. Thanks also to the opportunity provided by the Virtual Safety Car, they favoured a more measured management of pace and degradation, which allowed them to significantly extend stint lengths and made the one-stop strategy the preferred choice for the majority of the field.
P “The star of the Grand Prix was the Hard tyre, a compound that had been little explored during free practice and which today demonstrated a very high level of consistency, proving to be the most robust of the three compounds from both a thermal and mechanical perspective. With the C2, we saw several stints exceeding 45 laps, reaching very high levels of wear without any significant performance drop-off. Both the Medium and the Soft also proved to be effective options despite the track temperatures. The C4, in particular, completed competitive stints comparable to those of the Medium in terms of durability.
P “As expected, graining appeared mainly on the front-left tyre, on the inner area of the tread, but with limited intensity. The work carried out by the teams on car set-up and tyre management helped to minimise its effects. In a race characterised by few overtaking opportunities, the drivers were able to focus on tyre management, contributing to a very straightforward contest from a strategic perspective.
P “Congratulations to Ugo Ugochukwu for securing the Formula 3 championship title today at the end of a highly competitive season. The series continues to represent an important proving ground for young talents from all over the world. The fact that the title was decided only at the final round highlights the exceptionally high level of competitiveness within the championship, which this year delivered spectacular racing and outstanding sporting value.”

H1 What the teams said – Race day in Spain
P The drivers and teams report back on all the action from the Madring for the Spanish Grand Prix.
H3 Mercedes
P Kimi Antonelli got a great start from P2, but when challenging for the lead cut the apex of the corner and was forced to cede position. His attempts to do so were messy and he briefly fell behind Verstappen until the Dutchman had to do the same thing. That left Antonelli second, a few seconds behind race leader Norris. But when the Italian got a cheap pit stop under the VSC, he became the de facto leader and from there he kept his race pretty clean to take his eighth win of the year.
P As for George Russell, he had contact with Piastri at the start but was lucky to hold on to P6. The team opted to pit him under the VSC too, even though he started on the hards, and then did not think the mediums would last so pitted Russell a second time. That dropped him back again, and he finished fifth.
P Kimi Antonelli, 1st
P "It was great to get the victory today, but we know we were a little bit fortunate with the timing of the Virtual Safety Car. Lando (Norris) was in control at the front, but we were able to dive into the pits just as the Virtual Safety Car was deployed, make the cheap stop onto the Hard, get the net lead and run to the end. We probably didn’t deserve to win therefore but we will of course take it.
P "We can also be happy with our pace today. We know we are still out of step with other teams in terms of upgrades, but we have been able to win the last two races at very different circuits. That is encouraging as we continue the season; we have a good position in the championships but we know there is still a very long way to go."
P George Russell, 5th
P "No matter what we had done with strategy today we would have finished P5. The Virtual Safety Car came at the worst point for everyone who had started on the Hard tyre like me, and the best point for those who had started on the Medium. Unfortunately, that is how racing goes sometimes but it is a little bit the story of my season so far! It was very difficult to overtake today but I’ve enjoyed driving the Madring overall this weekend.
P "It is going to be an intense run to the end of the season. I’m looking forward to getting back to the factory, working with the team, and getting ready for the first of three triple-headers. My pace today, particularly on the Hard tyre, felt good so we can be encouraged by that as we head to Baku."
P Toto Wolff, Head of Mercedes-Benz Motorsport
P "We are pleased to have taken the first victory at the Madring; it has been another successful new event for F1 at a great location. Kimi drove well and, whilst the Virtual Safety Car played into his hands, he drove well to bring the car home at what has proved to be a very challenging circuit. To take another win at such a different track to Monza, having not brought a major update package to the car since Canada, is very encouraging.
P "On George’s side, he was slightly unfortunate with the timing of the Virtual Safety Car. We started him on the Hard tyre, intending to go long, but we had to take the cheap stop under the Virtual Safety Car and to do something different if we were to try and beat Leclerc. The Ferrari stayed out and we switch George to the Medium but unfortunately it wasn’t the strongest tyre today. George reported early on that he was suffering so we went back to the Hard compound; ultimately whatever we had done we would have come home P5 today.
P "We now have one week to get ready for Baku and the beginning of the first of three triple-headers. Extending our lead in the championships is good but we know there is still so much racing to come. It is going to be an intense run to the end of the season but we’re excited for that challenge."
P Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director
P "That was a great result for Kimi and a really strong weekend for the team. We clearly benefited from the timing of the Virtual Safety Car, but credit goes to the drivers and everyone in the garage for being ready to react. The execution of both stops was excellent and that helped us take the win today.
P "For Kimi, the decision to pit under the Virtual Safety Car was the one that ultimately put him in the net lead of the race. George's situation was a little more complicated. We had elected to do the opposite of Leclerc strategically because, when you're behind, you often need to try something different to create an opportunity. As the race unfolded, though, it became clear that the Hard tyre was performing better than we had expected and was the compound to be on. That said, if we had mirrored the Ferrari’s strategy, we would have still likely finished P5 with overtaking proving so difficult.
P "Ultimately, the Virtual Safety Car arrived at the perfect moment for the cars that could switch onto the Hard tyre, and that's sometimes how racing goes. The important thing is that we've come away with a race win, a strong points haul, and strengthened our position in both championships.
P "We'll regroup over the next few days and prepare for the run to the finish of the season. Nine races in 11 weeks is going to be a demanding stretch for everyone, but we've put ourselves in a good position in both title fights and we'll keep pushing right to the final Grand Prix."
H3 Red Bull
P Max Verstappen cut the corner at Turn 2 when fighting with Hamilton, and was even briefly ahead of Antonelli. But the team told him to give the positions back, which after Hamilton retired left him third. The Dutchman benefitted from a VSC pit stop to jump ahead of Norris, and managed to catch Antonelli to show the RB22 had some good race pace. He kept a charging Norris at bay in the closing stages for his second straight rostrum.
P As for Liam Lawson, he ran a long stint on the hards, and had to fight hard to come home sixth. He could not keep a fresher shod Russell at bay, but did manage to overtake Gasly before a lonely end to his race.
P Max Verstappen, 2nd
P “It was a great result, and we really maximised our performance, with finishing P2 on this track a solid way to wrap up a good weekend. At the start, Lewis clipped the kerb and jumped back onto the racing line, I had to go off track, otherwise both of us would have taken damage. I don't think we had the pace to challenge for the lead anyway, Kimi and Lando were faster than me throughout, so I'm happy with second. It's a circuit that's very difficult to pass on; if you position yourself in the middle, there isn't really a way through, so I was able to hold off Lando until the end. This double header has been a positive one. The car has been in a decent window both weekends, and we've been able to score consistently good points over the last few races. A podium is a nice way to end the European swing."
P Liam Lawson, 6th
P "I think it was a decent race. We had good speed through parts of it, but I just think we weren’t on the ideal strategy today. We went for the alternate strategy, starting on the Hards. At the start I lost the position to Franco and lost a lot of time as it was, but by the time I cleared him the VSC came out and they’d boxed, so it was just tricky from there. The start was exciting and I had to take a lot of risks to get the move done on Franco because it’s quite difficult to overtake here. It would’ve been nice to start a bit higher, but considering where we did start, the result today was good and I’m happy we managed to gain two places in the Race. I’m much more confident in the car this week, we’ve made a couple of great steps, so there are some good things to take away from the weekend."
P Laurent Mekies, Team Principal
P “After Monza another strong result from the whole Team at the end of a tough race. Once again, Max extracted absolutely everything from the car, as he always does. There was obviously some frustration at the start when he had to give the place back to Lewis, but the Team on the pit wall took a good look at it and, credit to them, made the difficult call. It was painful at the time, but Max immediately got himself back into the fight and was outstanding all the way to the flag, including a great defence against the McLaren in the final laps.
P "It was also a strong race and some good points from Liam. It certainly wasn’t easy towards the end of his first stint on worn Hard tyres, but he kept his cool and showed good pace in the final stint.
P "Max’s P2 is his fifth podium in the last seven races and, although we have had a couple of tricky moments along the way, we are continuing to close the gap and credit needs to go to everyone working behind the scenes at Milton Keynes, improving every aspect of the car and its PU.”
H3 McLaren
P Lando Norris had a great start from pole and after some early shenanigans with track limits, settled into the lead. He built a decent gap to Antonelli behind but when a VSC was called he was already past the pit lane entry. As such, Antonelli and Verstappen behind pitted for a cheap stop. By the time Norris came around, the VSC had ended – and then he had a slow pit stop to boot, which dropped him down the order.
P The reigning World Champion did well to fight back to the podium, but luck was not on his side today. Nor was it on Oscar Piastri’s, who suffered front wing damage after being squeezed by Russell off the line. That dropped him out of the top 10, but he ran a long first stint to fight back, and pulled off some overtakes to at least finish in the points.
P Lando Norris, 3rd
P “I feel like I drove a perfect race today, my tyre management was very strong, and I felt a step ahead of everyone. Qualifying was perfect, the race in terms of performance was perfect, and we were quickest by a big margin. It's just incredibly frustrating to lose in a way that has nothing to do with performance. I was the only driver on the whole grid who didn't get a pit stop under the VSC, and I lost around twenty seconds of race time because of it.
P “There are still positives to take from this weekend in terms of what we can do. The pace on Sunday is clearly there, we were better than everyone today, and that's reassuring. Saturday is still an area we need to improve, but if we can close that gap and avoid situations like today, we win. We'll take today on the chin, keep pushing, and go again.”
P Oscar Piastri, 8th
P “It was a tough one for us today, and a pretty painful race from start to finish. I got squeezed by Russell which then broke my front wing on the first lap, and from there we just got stuck in traffic, which is tricky with the lack of overtaking here. Unfortunately, the VSC timing wasn't ideal for the Hard tyre starters like myself. When we did pit, the Mediums didn't perform how we wanted them to, and I was back in traffic.
P “The positive we can take is that there are some good learnings, especially on how to get the most out of the car. We also had some decent pace on the Hard tyre in clean air, which is always encouraging. We will review, see what more we can learn and then and take it into the next part of the season.”
P Andrea Stella, Team Principal
P “Today is a day of mixed emotions, but we leave with our heads held high and a smile on our faces. Lando was the fastest driver on track and absolutely deserved the victory. The pace we showed was phenomenal, especially at a circuit where we didn't expect to be so strong. Unfortunately, factors entirely outside our control, specifically the timing of the Virtual Safety Car, meant the win was taken from us. We reviewed all options, but the circumstances left us with no viable alternative strategy. It's frustrating when you have the performance to win and the racing gods aren't on your side, but we will take it on the chin.
P “The biggest positive is the clear evidence that our car is competitive and capable of fighting at the front. The team did an exceptional job all weekend to unlock this level of performance, and it gives us great confidence for the upcoming races. We are closing the gap in the championship and have proven we can be a threat on Sundays. While it was a tougher day for Oscar, who was compromised by damage at the start, we are working hard with him to unlock his full potential. We look forward to Baku, ready to fight for podiums and victories.”
H3 Ferrari
P Lewis Hamilton was fighting with Verstappen at the start, but his race unravelled soon after when a brake issue forced him to pit to retire the car, his first DNF of the season. That left Charles Leclerc to fly the flag for Ferrari, which he did in style. On the hard tyre, he ran an exceptionally long opening stint to lead the race for much of the afternoon. But with no more disruptions, he eventually did have to pit under normal race conditions, which dropped him to fourth.
P Lewis Hamilton, DNF
P "Firstly, a big thank you to the team for the job they did throughout the weekend. We were in a position to fight for a strong result and the car had been performing well.
P "Unfortunately, we encountered an issue with the braking system very quickly into the race which brought our afternoon to an early end. It’s disappointing, especially considering all the effort that went into the weekend both here at the track and back at the factory. We will turn our attention to the next race and do our best to come back strong there."
P Charles Leclerc, 4th
P "The race was good and we brought home what was realistically the best result possible, given that this track is so difficult to overtake on. We did a good job with the strategy, playing our cards to suit our situation. We decided to take our chance and wait for a Safety Car to come up before the end of the race to gain an advantage, but it didn’t play out that way in the end. If we had been on the opposite strategy, I would have finished fourth as well, so either way, we extracted the most we could out of our race.
P "Now we take a break and reset ahead of the next round in Baku, a track I’ve always enjoyed racing on in the past."
P Fred Vasseur, Team Principal
P "Like a few other teams, we split the strategy today, starting one car on the Soft compound and the other on the Hard. With Charles, we were leading the group that started on the Hard tyre and he drove a very strong first stint, pushing for almost 50 laps while maintaining good pace throughout.
P "We knew there was a reasonable chance of a Safety Car or a red flag, so we decided to extend the stint and keep that opportunity open. A red flag could have put us in a position to fight for the win, while a late Safety Car could have given us a shot at third. In the end neither happened, but I think it was absolutely worth trying and Charles delivered a very solid performance. As for Lewis, at this stage we don’t yet know the exact cause of the brake system issue that forced him to retire and we will investigate it thoroughly. Regarding the championship, our approach remains the same: we take it one race at a time, and our focus now turns to Baku."
H3 Alpine
P Franco Colapinto made a great start to pick up a couple of places and run solidly in the top 10. He pitted under the VSC which dropped him back, but the Argentinian racer was happy to bide his time and work his way back up the order. His team mate ran the longest first stint of anyone on the hard tyres, eventually pitting on the penultimate lap. Pierre Gasly had hung it out in the hopes of a Safety Car, but that stop dropped him out of the points and he was handed a five-second penalty for speeding in the pit lane too.
P Pierre Gasly, 12th
